## AI Learning Series

Learning AI Inference as a Distributed Systems Engineer — 30 posts published (Day 0–29 of 150). Topics: KV cache, continuous batching, GPU scheduling, RAG pipelines, feature flags for model rollouts, eBPF tracing, OTel Collector, LLM observability, agent infrastructure.

- [Day 84 — Health Checks for Model Endpoints — Active Probes](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-84-active-health-probes-circuit-breaker.html): Active probes vs passive metrics, the Closed/Open/HalfOpen circuit breaker behind fallback-chain's health checks, and why the Redis-backed unhealthy set needs TTL refresh so a crashed monitor fails open.
- [Day 83 — Streaming Token Delivery — Backpressure Basics](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-83-streaming-backpressure-buffer-size.html): Buffer size ties to TTFB vs memory — the TCP receive-window analogy for a streaming proxy's backpressure, and why fallback-chain's ChunkRelay gets it for free from a blocking read-write-flush loop instead of a goroutine and a channel.
- [Day 82 — Measuring Proxy Overhead — p99, Not Mean](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-82-measuring-proxy-overhead-p99-not-mean.html): Why fallback-chain's under-10ms streaming-proxy target has to be measured as a p99 from a merged latency histogram, not a running average, before Day 83's real number means anything.
- [Day 81 — Fallback Chains — Graceful Degradation in Inference](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-81-fallback-chains-graceful-degradation.html): An ordered ModelRef chain with a widening 2s/5s/8s timeout budget, a three-state circuit breaker that costs zero timeout on a known-down endpoint, and a chunked streaming proxy targeting under 10ms added latency.
- [Day 80 — Multi-Objective Routing — Scalarization and Weights](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-80-multi-objective-routing-scalarization.html): RouteIQ's decision.Utility scalarizes quality, cost, and latency into one ranked value via tenant-overridable weights — the same technique a cost-aware load balancer uses — plus why the tie-break toward the cheaper model exists.
- [Day 79 — Score Normalization — Why 0–1 Beats Raw Likert](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-79-score-normalization-0-1-vs-likert.html): Converting rubric.WeightedScore's raw 0-100 output into a comparable 0-1 unit (a z-score DS analogy), plus the 30-sample statistical noise floor that decides how much to trust a 1h/24h rollup bucket's mean.
- [Day 78 — Async Evaluation Pipelines — Throughput Over Latency](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-78-async-evaluation-pipelines-throughput-over-latency.html): Batching judge calls that share one resolved rubric template, a bounded single retry instead of a retry loop, a trailing-window circuit breaker per task_type, and four distinct DLQ reasons so a judge_unavailable sample is never averaged in as a real score.
- [Day 77 — LLM-as-Judge — Rubrics as Structured Data](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-77-judge-rubrics-structured-data.html): A JudgeRubric is a versioned JSON schema with weighted criteria, the same contract-first shape as an ingest event — why Haiku grades instead of the model being judged, and why quality scores aggregate per tenant x task_type rather than into one global average.
- [Day 76 — Exact-Match vs Semantic Cache — Two-Tier Memory Hierarchy](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-76-two-tier-cache-hierarchy.html): Why prompt-fingerprinter's exact-match L1 sits in front of semantic-cache-engine's embedding-based L2 — the same cheap-narrow-first shape a CPU's L1/L2 memory hierarchy uses — and how today's admin API makes L1's definition of "duplicate" tenant-configurable.
- [Day 75 — Prompt Fingerprinting — Canonical Forms Before Hashing](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-75-canonical-forms-before-hashing.html): How prompt-fingerprinter normalizes a request into canonical form before hashing it, so byte-different-but-equivalent prompts still collide into the same cache key.
- [Day 74 — Quality Scorer Preview](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-74-quality-scorer-preview.html): A router that only weighs cost and latency is missing a signal — model-quality-scorer previews how quality joins the formula, scored asynchronously off the request path.
- [Day 73 — Collision Handling](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-73-collision-handling.html): A hash-keyed cache can't detect a collision — the fix is the same shape as a rare UUID collision: scope the key, and bound how long you trust it.
- [Day 72 — L1/L2 Stack Design](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-72-l1-l2-stack-design.html): A CPU never reports one blended cache-hit number across L1/L2/L3 — a Redis-then-pgvector prompt cache needs the identical per-level accounting, plus a backfill policy a fixed hardware hierarchy never needed.
- [Day 71 — Canonicalization Rules](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-71-canonicalization-rules.html): Whitespace collapse and sorted JSON keys are the same rules Git uses to hash a commit and AWS uses to sign a request — canonicalization is older than LLM caching, just applied to a prompt now.
- [Day 70 — Prompt Fingerprints](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-70-prompt-fingerprints.html): Exact cache is dedup at ingress. A SHA-256 fingerprint of a canonical prompt answers "have I seen this exact request" in under a millisecond, before any embedding call runs.
- [Day 69 — Failure Policies for Budget Redis](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-69-failure-policies-for-budget-redis.html): Document the outage mode — auditors will ask. Fail-open and fail-closed are both legitimate policies for a dependency check guarding a costly operation; the general pattern behind cost-budget-enforcer's per-tenant Redis outage policy.
- [Day 68 — Gateway Middleware Ordering](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-68-gateway-middleware-ordering.html): Order matters — wrong order leaks spend. Why budget-then-cache-then-model is the only ordering of a stub gateway's three stages that makes "a blocked request costs zero" provably true, verified with a spy on the downstream calls, not just the final response.
- [Day 67 — Live Config for Spend](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-67-live-config-for-spend.html): Budget PATCH is a feature flag for money — mutating an in-memory config store and a Kafka topic with no shared transaction is a saga (local transaction + compensating action), not a distributed-lock problem.
- [Day 66 — Hard vs Soft Limits](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-66-hard-vs-soft-limits.html): Block vs downgrade — why one threshold can't do a rate limiter's whole job, and why the 100%-to-120% soft-to-hard gap is sized as deliberate runway for the fallback path to actually run.
- [Day 65 — Token Budgets as Rate Limits](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-65-token-budgets-as-rate-limits.html): Lua atomicity again — budgets race like rate limits, but the algorithm underneath a budget answers a different question than ingestion's existing token bucket. A token bucket bounds a rate; a sliding-window counter bounds a total, and the two aren't interchangeable.
- [Day 64 — Load Testing ANN](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-64-load-testing-ann.html): Same k6 discipline as ingestion — p99 under SLA. A closed-loop harness measures whether an index's own query cost is within budget; coordinated omission is why its p99 is a lower bound, not the whole story.
- [Day 63 — Cache Quality Metrics](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-63-cache-quality-metrics.html): a hit rate alone tells you how often the cache fired, never whether firing was correct — precision, recall, and a threshold-sweep tool that makes the tradeoff visible instead of assumed.
- [Day 62 — ANN Search at QPS](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-62-ann-search-at-qps.html): IVFFlat vs HNSW is a MergeTree-ORDER-BY-shaped decision — made once, expensive to change, and the thing that determines whether a nearest-neighbor query is fast for the life of the table.
- [Day 61 — Embedding Pipelines](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-61-embedding-pipelines.html): prompt_hash idempotency is Kafka exactly-once for vectors — batching amortizes an embedding API's fixed cost, and idempotency is what makes that batching safe to retry or replay as a backfill.
- [Day 60 — Semantic Caching Economics](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-60-semantic-caching-economics.html): Sweep 0.88 to 0.96 on real prompts and plot dollars, not hit-rate vibes — a false-positive cache hit and a false-negative miss don't cost the same amount, so the threshold that maximizes hit rate rarely maximizes savings.
- [Day 59 — TraceForge — Agent Observability Is Distributed Tracing With Money on the Line](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-59-traceforge-agent-observability-distributed-tracing-money.html): Collector, analyzer, replay, benchmark — Month 2's product essay: an agent trace matters because every step on it can be billed to a tenant, and one dropped column can hide that bill from the dashboard meant to show it.
- [Day 58 — Month 2 Synthesis — Agents Are Distributed Systems](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-58-month-2-synthesis-agents-are-distributed-systems.html): Collector, analyzer, replay, benchmark — four weeks collapse into one thesis: an agent trace is a distributed transaction log, and every DS technique (idempotency, replay, divergence detection, backpressure) applies to it directly.
- [Day 57 — Launch Narrative — Benchmark as Hero Demo](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-57-launch-narrative-benchmark-as-hero-demo.html): 14 vs 9 resolves in one glance; the JSON report behind it does not. The landing page reuses report.Build's Day-53 headline instead of inventing a launch-tuned summary, so the launch artifact and the debugging report never quietly drift apart.
- [Day 56 — Monorepo vs Multi-Repo — Platform Packaging](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-56-monorepo-vs-multi-repo-platform-packaging.html): A per-component Dockerfile proves a component builds in isolation; only a shared docker-compose.yml proves four TraceForge components work together — and building it forced agent-benchmark-runner's first CLI.
- [Day 55 — Cross-Product Metrics — LensAI × TraceForge](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-55-cross-product-metrics-lensai-x-traceforge.html): agent-benchmark-runner's new LensAI ingest integration reuses LensAI's exact envelope instead of inventing its own — a join key decided before there's data to migrate, and a schema that's additive-safe only because of a property of today's Rust struct, not a contract either dual-writer enforces.
- [Day 54 — Flame Graphs — CPU Profile for Agents](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-54-flame-graphs-cpu-profile-for-agents.html): A CPU flame graph answers "which function ate the time" with one dimension — box width. agent-benchmark-runner's new flame graph timeline applies the same discipline to tool-call dollar cost instead, so the widest, hottest box is where the budget died.
- [Day 53 — Human-Readable Benchmark Reports](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-53-human-readable-benchmark-reports.html): A compare.Result is a Go struct nobody reads directly — agent-benchmark-runner's report generator turns it into a headline that leads with divergence ("14 calls vs 9, diverged at step 5") plus markdown, JSON, and an SVG timeline for three different readers.
- [Day 52 — Statistical Rigor — N Runs, Confidence](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-52-statistical-rigor-n-runs-confidence.html): agent-benchmark-runner's orchestrator runs a task N times under bounded concurrency with per-repetition derived seeds, and reports a pass rate with a 95% Wilson confidence interval plus median/P95 step count instead of a single pass/fail bit.
- [Day 51 — Benchmark Methodology for Agents](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-51-benchmark-methodology-for-agents.html): agent-benchmark-runner fixes the task, seed, and tool list as data before comparing two agents, and grades runs with a closed set of typed criteria instead of a non-deterministic LLM judge.
- [Day 50 — Operability — CLI as API](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-50-operability-cli-as-api.html): replay and diff share one contract — same input shape, same output shape, same exit-code convention — verified by a smoke test that checks the interface a human and a CI job both rely on, not the replay logic underneath it.
- [Day 49 — Streaming Parsers — OOM-Safe Debugging](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-49-streaming-parsers-oom-safe-debugging.html): eventlog.Scanner streams a shared trace log one line at a time instead of buffering the whole file, and the honest benchmark against the old batch path shows streaming trading speed and allocations for bounded peak memory, not a free win.
- [Day 48 — Fault Injection for Tool RPCs](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-48-fault-injection-for-tool-rpcs.html): pkg/fault defines synthetic timeout, 500, and stale-cache failures, and ToolMocker.Inject forces a chosen replay step to fail with one of them — checked before the frozen-response lookup — so an agent's error-handling path can be verified on demand instead of waiting for it to happen live.
- [Day 47 — Diff Semantics — Structural vs Textual](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-47-diff-semantics-structural-vs-textual.html): pkg/diff compares two agent traces on ToolName + InputHash — the same composite key pkg/mocker already used — instead of diffing raw JSON text, and returns the first tool_call step where the two traces structurally disagree.
- [Day 46 — Deterministic Mocks — Record and Replay](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-46-deterministic-mocks-record-and-replay.html): ToolMocker keys frozen tool responses on (tool_name, input_hash) so two tools with identical input never collide, and replay.Run walks the recorded tool_call sequence with an optional --stop-at-step halt for inspecting a run mid-flight.
- [Day 45 — Object Storage Economics for Traces](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-45-object-storage-economics-for-traces.html): pkg/export compresses event logs with zstd, checksums the compressed bytes, and classifies objects into hot/cold/expired retention tiers — tested entirely against an in-memory ObjectStore fake, no live MinIO required.
- [Day 44 — Event Sourcing for Agent Runs](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-44-event-sourcing-agent-runs.html): pkg/eventlog's append-only log and the ToolMocker that freezes tool responses — Kafka log compaction as the DS analogy for deterministic agent replay.
- [Day 43 — Backpressure on Analytics Pipelines](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-43-backpressure-analytics-pipelines.html): Splitting tool-spans from tool-stats keeps a slow ClickHouse aggregator from ever stalling span ingest — consumer lag as the health signal, and a chaos test that proves zero spans drop.
- [Day 42 — Unified Billing Events — One Envelope](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-42-unified-billing-events-one-envelope.html): A single BillingEvent envelope, keyed on tenant_id and trace_id, joins inference and tool cost into one table — fire-and-forget dual-write in Go, one query, both sources.
- [Day 41 — Cost Waterfalls — CFO-Friendly Visuals](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-41-cost-waterfalls-cfo-friendly-visuals.html): Exclusive time, bottleneck ranking, and the ClickHouse-to-Grafana pipeline that turns per-tool cost into a chart a team acts on instead of a table it debates.
- [Day 40 — Graph Algorithms on Traces](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-40-graph-algorithms-on-traces.html): Modeling a trace as a directed graph — DFS cycle detection, Kahn's-algorithm topological sort, and the N+1 lint rule agents have never had.
- [Day 39 — Exclusive Time vs Wall Time](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-39-exclusive-time-wall-time.html): Why summing span durations double-counts, and why the tool-duration alert divides by trace wall time instead.
- [Day 29 — The AI Infrastructure Stack — Full Map](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-29-ai-infrastructure-stack-full-map.html): Five layers from training pipeline to agent orchestration — where each is hard and where LensAI fits.
- [Day 28 — Competitor Teardown: LensAI Positioning](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-28-competitor-teardown-lensai-positioning.html): Honest teardown of Datadog LLM Observability, Helicone, and Langfuse — where each falls short.
- [Day 27 — OpenTelemetry Collector as Integration Hub](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-27-opentelemetry-collector-integration-hub.html): Processors as middleware, exporters as adapters, and why LensAI speaks OTel natively.
- [Day 26 — Fine-Tuning vs RAG vs Prompting — Infra Cost View](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-26-fine-tuning-rag-prompting-infra-cost.html): Four-question decision framework and cost crossover at three traffic volumes.
- [Day 25 — Cost Models for LLM Gateways](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-25-cost-models-llm-gateways.html): Cache hit rate × cheaper model route × prompt cache — token economics for model routing.
- [Day 24 — GPU Scheduling as Resource Management](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-24-gpu-scheduling-resource-management.html): MIG, tensor parallelism, and Kubernetes extended resources.
- [Day 23 — Evaluations as Event Streams](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-23-evaluations-as-event-streams.html): LLM-as-judge as a Kafka producer, eval event schema, and the ClickHouse join that closes the cost-quality loop.
- [Day 22 — Feature Flags for Model Rollouts](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-22-feature-flags-model-rollouts.html): Deterministic hashing, audit logs, and the four-step canary sequence.
- [Day 21 — Production Reliability for LLM APIs](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-21-production-reliability-llm-apis.html): Four-bucket error classification — retry, circuit break, fallback, fail loud.
- [Day 20 — Prompt Engineering as Infra Optimization](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-20-prompt-engineering-infra-optimization.html): Prompt cache and prefix reuse in dollars per million requests.
- [Day 19 — Agent Infrastructure — Tools, Memory, Loops](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-19-agent-infrastructure-tools-memory-loops.html): Tool calling as RPC with hallucination risk, agent memory as tiered cache.
- [Day 18 — Quantization and Model Optimization](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-18-quantization-model-optimization.html): GPTQ vs AWQ vs bitsandbytes — pick variants like a codec picks compression.
- [Day 17 — LLM Observability: What Actually Matters](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-17-llm-observability-what-actually-matters.html): Arize vs Langfuse vs Helicone schema diff against eBPF-captured events.
- [Day 16 — The Mental Model That Made LLM Infra Click](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-16-the-mental-model-llm-infra-click.html): Prefill as batch write, decode as serial consumer.
- [Day 15 — Multi-Model Routing Strategies](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-15-multi-model-routing-strategies.html): Cost-first vs quality-first vs latency-first routing.
- [Day 14 — eBPF for AI Infrastructure](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-14-ebpf-for-ai-infrastructure.html): Zero-SDK LLM HTTP tracing via eBPF — kernel probes vs SDK patches.
- [Day 13 — Embeddings as Dense Time-Series IDs](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-13-embeddings-as-dense-time-series-ids.html): Embedding pipeline as event stream, model version migration, blue/green index cutover.
- [Day 12 — Embeddings as Dense Time-Series IDs (Part 1)](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-12-embeddings-as-dense-time-series-ids.html): Vectors are high-cardinality series in ANN storage engines.
- [Day 11 — Semantic Caching vs Exact-Match Redis](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-11-semantic-caching-vs-exact-match-redis.html): Exact Redis when bytes are the contract; semantic cache when paraphrase is the traffic.
- [Day 10 — Serving Frameworks Compared as Queue Schedulers](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-10-serving-frameworks-queue-schedulers.html): vLLM vs TGI vs Ollama on admission and continuous batching.
- [Day 9 — GPU Memory Management](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-9-gpu-memory-management.html): Four VRAM tenants, one capacity plan.
- [Day 8 — RAG as an Infrastructure Pipeline](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-8-rag-as-infra-pipeline.html): Five pipeline stages, one latency budget.

- [Day 6 — Quantization vs Compression Tradeoffs](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-6-quantization-vs-compression-tradeoffs.html): INT8/INT4 as Snappy-vs-Zstd for weights.
- [Day 5 — Sampling and Deterministic Routing](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-5-sampling-deterministic-routing.html): Head vs tail sampling, hash(trace_id) discipline.
- [Day 4 — Tensor Parallelism Meets Kafka Partitions](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-4-tensor-parallelism-kafka-partitions.html): TP/PP scale-out, Triton as routing table.

- [Day 1 — The KV Cache Is a Memory Bandwidth Problem](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-1-kv-cache-memory-bandwidth.html): Prefill vs decode, why decode is memory-bound.
- [Day 0 — Why I'm Writing This Series](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/ai-learning/day-0-series-roadmap.html): Distributed-systems lens on AI inference — 150-day scope and format.

## Experience Series

Production war stories from large-scale engineering: Agoda (WhiteFalcon in-house TSDB, 1.5T events/day), Delivery Hero (rider tracking at 5k geo-events/s), Wayfair (pricing platform, 70k+ suppliers), Walmart Labs (7M+ IoT sensors, 50+ facilities).

- [Day 84 — BrowserStack Integration Test Flakiness — Health Checks That Lied](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-84-browserstack-health-checks-that-lied.html): A green /health endpoint kept passing while the CI device-instrumentation pipeline it guarded had quietly stopped serving — why a liveness check and a working dependency are two different claims.
- [Day 83 — Agoda Cross-Tier Read Latency — Snappy Hot, Zstd Cold](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-83-cold-tier-compression-snappy-to-zstd.html): Migrating WhiteFalcon's cold-tier Parquet compression from Snappy to Zstd cut storage 18% with under 1% average read-latency impact — verified at the percentile level, not just the mean, by reusing the existing cross-tier histogram merge.
- [Day 82 — Delivery Hero OSRM Pool Saturation — PDBs vs. the Lunch Rush](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-82-osrm-pool-saturation-pdb-tradeoffs.html): An OSRM connection pool sized for the average hour hit an 8% error burn at lunch rush, and the fix — scaling Route Consumers out — was blocked by a PodDisruptionBudget tuned for routine node rotation until minAvailable became a floor that scales with HPA's desired replica count.
- [Day 81 — Wayfair Sub-Second SKU Propagation — Event Ordering](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-81-sub-second-sku-propagation-event-ordering.html): The pricing_refresh partition key already put every SKU's price changes in Kafka order, but shadow-mode testing found a retry path where a stale batch computation could still publish after a live correction — fixed with a version stamped at computation start, not publish time.
- [Day 80 — Route Revisions and Revisit Order System — Compensating Bad Polylines](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-80-route-revisions-revisit-order-system.html): Delivery Hero's Route Service recomputes 5k+ polylines a second, and Revisit Order System handles a stale route by producing a new immutable revision instead of mutating the existing Route object in place.
- [Day 79 — Walmart Stream Analytics Dropped Messages — Switching to Kafka](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-79-stream-analytics-to-kafka.html): A windowed Azure Stream Analytics query has no memory past its own close boundary, so a burst of reconnecting WeIoT sensors could push events past the window before they were processed. Migrating to Kafka's replayable, offset-addressed log fixed it, verified with dual-write and a deliberate consumer-recovery drill before cutover.
- [Day 78 — Delivery Hero Async Pipelines — Why We Decoupled SQS from OSRM](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-78-decoupling-sqs-from-osrm.html): Rider notification delivery used to share a call chain with OSRM route recompute, so a throttled notification provider could stall routing for every rider behind it. An SQS-boundary decoupling with a shadow-mode rollout got to 5k+ route updates/sec and sub-second delivery status.
- [Day 77 — Agoda P99 Cannot Be Averaged Across Tenants](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-77-p99-per-tenant-slos.html): WhiteFalcon's cross-tier quantile merge fixed hot/cold P95 disagreement. It didn't fix a platform review asking for one blended P99 across tenants — which would have hidden a real SLO breach behind everyone else's healthy traffic.
- [Day 76 — Supplier API Circuit Breakers — Half-Open State in Production](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-76-circuit-breaker-half-open-state.html): The trip condition on Wayfair's supplier pricing circuit breaker shipped years ago. What got tested on purpose, for the first time, ahead of Black Friday was the half-open recovery path.
- [Wayfair's Redis Lua Token Bucket at 250k SKU Scale](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-75-wayfair-redis-lua-token-bucket.html): Revisiting Wayfair's atomic Redis Lua rate limiter as the supplier catalog scaled past 250k+ SKUs per supplier, and how it rhymes with today's tenant-scoped cache-key design.
- [Day 74 — OTel for Cache Tiers](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-74-otel-for-cache-tiers.html): A Delivery Hero rider-tracking Revisit Order System answered "why this route" by replaying history after the fact. Draws on the OSRM-backed rider tracking pipeline (5k+ route updates/sec) at Delivery Hero.
- [Day 73 — Hash Collisions Happen](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-73-hash-collisions-happen.html): A short version fingerprint traded away collision resistance for a cheap on-device check at Walmart. Draws on the WeIoT SmartBuildings OTA firmware framework (7M+ sensors, 50+ facilities).
- [Day 72 — Two-Tier Cache Metrics](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-72-two-tier-cache-metrics.html): WhiteFalcon's Redis/Ceph split and prompt-fingerprinter's L1/L2 split ask the same question one layer apart: which tier did the work. Draws on ~5 months contributing to WhiteFalcon's cross-tier query engine at Agoda.
- [Day 71 — Normalization Is Contract Testing](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-71-normalization-is-contract-testing.html): A Bigtable row key and a prompt cache key make the same unenforced promise — every writer and reader must compute the identical canonical form, or the lookup silently misses. Draws on Wayfair's PAS pricing keyspace (250k+ SKU updates/supplier across 20k+ suppliers).
- [Day 70 — Exact Match Before Fuzzy](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-70-exact-match-before-fuzzy.html): A cheap exact check ahead of an expensive approximate one is the same tiering discipline WhiteFalcon's hot Redis tier and cold Ceph/S3 tier already run on at Agoda, applied to prompt-fingerprinter's new cache instead of a database.
- [Day 69 — Fail Closed vs Open — Pick and Document](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-69-fail-closed-vs-open-pick-and-document.html): Fail-open and fail-closed are both correct choices — for different tenants. Draws on WhiteFalcon's hot-tier Redis retention boundary at Agoda to make the case for cost-budget-enforcer's new per-tenant outage policy.
- [Day 68 — Stub Gateway — Compose Before Polish](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-68-stub-gateway-compose-before-polish.html): A pipeline's stage order has to be proven before any one stage gets optimized. Draws on an Agoda WhiteFalcon pipeline lineage extended (but not designed) to make the case for RouteIQ's own stub gateway.
- [Day 67 — Live Budget PATCH — Ops Can't Wait for Deploy](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-67-live-budget-patch-ops-cant-wait.html): A deploy gate does two jobs — validation and provenance — and a live-editable admin lever only earns the right to skip it by rebuilding both explicitly. Anchored on Delivery Hero's Global Logistics Platform.
- [Day 66 — Midnight Rollover Bugs](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-66-midnight-rollover-bugs.html): A window boundary anchored to whenever the first event after reset happens to arrive isn't a rounding error — it's a one-directional drift. Walmart WeIoT's daily telemetry rollups and today's cost-budget-enforcer window math hit the same bug class from opposite directions.
- [Day 65 — Token Budgets — Finance Meets Gateway](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-65-token-budgets-finance-meets-gateway.html): A hard reject-only guardrail and a silent no-op are both wrong for the same reason. Wayfair's UCMS base-cost violation flow and cost-budget-enforcer's three-threshold Redis design both pick a third option — degrade, don't just block.
- [Day 64 — pgvector Under Load](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-64-pgvector-under-load.html): An index's cost is never evenly spread across its keys — Agoda's RoaringBitmap cardinality incident and today's flat-load pgvector test share the same blind spot: skew, not the average, is what determines the tail.
- [Day 63 — Hit Rate Without Honesty Is Vanity](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-63-hit-rate-without-honesty-is-vanity.html): A cache hit-rate panel with no false-positive signal has the same blind spot as an Agoda Prometheus alert that went dark the moment cardinality exploded — a number that only counts successes can't tell you when it stops seeing the failure.
- [Day 62 — False Positives Have a Dollar Cost](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-62-false-positives-dollar-cost.html): A cache similarity threshold and OSRM's map-match confidence score both bet correctness against cost — semantic-cache-engine's 0.92 default and a false-positive budget make that bet measurable instead of just felt-safe.
- [Day 61 — Embeddings Are Batch Jobs](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-61-embeddings-are-batch-jobs.html): A batch-of-32 embedding worker and Agoda WhiteFalcon's hourly-to-daily compaction cadence solve the same amortization problem — idempotency is what makes both safe to retry.
- [Day 60 — Semantic Cache — Wayfair Pricing Deja Vu](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-60-semantic-cache-wayfair-pricing-deja-vu.html): Aletheia's exact-match price cache couldn't tell noise from signal in a 250k-update supplier feed — the same tolerance problem semantic-cache-engine's similarity threshold now solves for prompts.
- [Day 59 — TraceForge Launch — From Flight Recorder to Agent Ops](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-59-traceforge-launch-flight-recorder-to-agent-ops.html): A recorder only your own team reads can hide a dropped field for months — a launched one can't. Today's fix closes exactly that gap between agent-benchmark-runner and LensAI, and ships the Grafana dashboard that proves it.
- [Day 58 — TraceForge — Agents Need a Flight Recorder](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-58-traceforge-agents-need-a-flight-recorder.html): A flight recorder doesn't prevent the crash — Delivery Hero's postmortem habit of tracking where two systems stop agreeing shapes today's agent-benchmark-runner divergence rehearsal, one day before it has to survive a real launch.
- [Day 57 — Launch Week — Integration or Nothing](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-57-launch-week-integration-or-nothing.html): A screenshot only proves something rendered once. Agoda's go-live checklist for the cross-tier query engine required a rerun script instead of a picture — the same discipline today's TraceForge landing page is built to satisfy.
- [Day 56 — Org Boundaries — Public Platform Identity](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-56-org-boundaries-public-platform-identity.html): Wayfair's architecture diagram labels every subsystem with an owning team — today's unified docker-compose.yml is the same proof, at a much smaller scale, for a traceforge-dev org: the backing move that turns an org name from a label into something true.
- [Day 55 — Two Products, One Tenant Bill](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-55-two-products-one-tenant-bill.html): Wayfair's ScheduledReader Total Cost Engine joins three independent cost sources into one number before the price calculator ever sees them separately — agent-benchmark-runner's new LensAI integration sets up the same join for two TraceForge products, one tenant_id at a time.
- [Day 54 — Flame Graphs — LLM Time vs Tool Time](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-54-flame-graphs-llm-time-vs-tool-time.html): A Walmart Labs HVAC dashboard sized and colored by energy draw made one over-consuming actuator obvious where a uniform zone-status grid didn't — agent-benchmark-runner's new cost flame graph makes the same bet for tool-call spend.
- [Day 53 — 14 Calls vs 9 — The Report Hiring Managers Get](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-53-the-report-hiring-managers-get.html): A cross-tier query fix at Agoda that collapsed two manual queries into one merged request, and agent-benchmark-runner's new report generator, lead with the same kind of number — because the reader deciding whether the work mattered rarely reads the mechanism.
- [Day 52 — Parallel Runs — Respect the Rate Limit](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-52-parallel-runs-respect-the-rate-limit.html): Delivery Hero's OSRM routing cluster taught that unbounded fan-out turns a downstream capacity limit into your own outage — agent-benchmark-runner's orchestrator bounds benchmark-repetition concurrency with the same fixed-worker-pool discipline.
- [Day 51 — Benchmark Agents Like Load Tests](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-51-benchmark-agents-like-load-tests.html): Agoda's cross-tier percentile merge taught that statistics computed on different inputs don't combine — agent-benchmark-runner's task YAML applies the same discipline to comparing two agents honestly.
- [Day 50 — Copy-Paste Debuggability](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-50-copy-paste-debuggability.html): Circuit breakers at Wayfair and decoupled pipelines at Delivery Hero only paid off if on-call could act on them fast — the same lesson applied to agent-replay-engine's own debugging CLI: a seven-step runbook and a CI smoke test that keeps it honest.
- [Day 49 — Streaming Parser — Don't OOM the Debugger](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-49-streaming-parser-dont-oom-the-debugger.html): Agoda's WhiteFalcon query engine stays bounded-memory by merging histogram buckets instead of loading raw rows — the honest benchmark behind giving traceforge replay the same discipline, including where the streaming rewrite wasn't the clean win it first looked like.
- [Day 48 — Inject Timeout — Chaos for Tool RPCs](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-48-inject-timeout-chaos-for-tool-rpcs.html): Wayfair's supplier bulk-submission circuit breaker (20k+ suppliers, 99.99% availability) only earns its keep if it trips correctly before a real SPCS outage cascades — traceforge replay --inject-timeout forces an agent's tool call to fail the same way, on command.
- [Day 47 — Diff Two Traces — Git Blame for Agents](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-47-diff-two-traces-git-blame-for-agents.html): Delivery Hero route disputes needed the first diverging routing decision out of thousands of noisy GPS coordinates, not a full polyline diff — traceforge diff finds the first diverging tool-call step between two agent traces the same way.
- [Day 46 — Replay Step 6 — Stop Before the Blast Radius](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-46-replay-step-6-stop-before-blast-radius.html): Walmart WeIoT's OTA firmware framework rolled updates out to millions of devices in waves, stopping before the next wave instead of rolling back after — agent-replay-engine's new --stop-at-step flag applies the same wave-boundary discipline to replaying an agent run's tool-call steps.
- [Day 45 — S3 for Traces — Compliance and Cost](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-45-s3-for-traces-compliance-and-cost.html): WhiteFalcon's Ceph→S3→Hadoop cold tier existed for audit as much as cost — agent-replay-engine's zstd + checksum + 30/90-day retention export applies the same tiering discipline to trace event logs at a fraction of the scale.
- [Day 44 — Event Sourcing — But the Events Hallucinate](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-44-event-sourcing-events-hallucinate.html): Wayfair PAS pricing simulations froze supplier costs and replayed them through a stateless pricing engine — and why agent-replay-engine's single-enforcement-point ToolMocker beats the pricing simulation's scattered snapshot timestamps.
- [Day 43 — Kafka as Shock Absorber — Again](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-43-kafka-shock-absorber-again.html): Agoda WhiteFalcon's Kafka pipeline absorbed every Redis slowdown as consumer lag, never data loss — the same shock absorber shape proven by a chaos test in tool-call-analyzer.
- [Day 42 — One Dashboard for Inference and Tools](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-42-one-dashboard-inference-tools.html): Agoda WhiteFalcon's Scala query engine merged Redis and S3 into one query face — the same one-dashboard-two-pipelines shape now joins tool-call-analyzer and LensAI on tenant_id.
- [Day 41 — Exclusive Time — Flame Graphs for Money](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-41-exclusive-time-flame-graphs-for-money.html): Delivery Hero's 340ms OSRM ETA pipeline hid its real bottleneck in an uninstrumented span — exclusive time found it, the same formula tool-call-analyzer now runs on every trace.
- [Day 40 — N+1 Tool Calls — The SELECT * of Agents](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-40-n1-tool-calls-select-star-of-agents.html): Walmart's Azure IoT Hub fan-out at 7M sensors, the edge pre-aggregation fix, and why agent tool calls need the same fix.
- [Day 39 — The Tool That Ate Your Margin](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-39-tool-ate-your-margin.html): Agoda cardinality attribution mapped onto tool-call-analyzer's cost rollup — same GROUP BY, different bill.
- [Day 29 — Thirty Days of Building — What Shipped vs What Matters](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-29-thirty-days-lensai-month-one.html): LensAI month-one retrospective — four repos, one smoke test, three things to redo.
- [Day 28 — Integration Tests — The Only Launch Criteria I Trust](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/experience/day-28-integration-tests-launch-criteria.html): Agoda staging discipline mapped to LensAI's smoke test launch gate.

## LensAI — Open Source Project

LensAI is zero-SDK AI inference observability: eBPF hooks TLS at the kernel level to capture LLM API calls without modifying application code. Cost attribution via resolved_model_id (what flagd actually routed vs what the app requested). Stack: Rust + Kafka + ClickHouse + Grafana.

- [Building a Production-Grade AI Inference Observability Pipeline](https://akshantvats.github.io/Profile/blog/series/inference-ai-project/building-ai-inference-observability.html): Architecture, tradeoffs, benchmarks.
- GitHub repos: https://github.com/AkshantVats/infra-ai-streaming (Rust ingest), https://github.com/AkshantVats/ebpf-llm-tracer (eBPF tracer), https://github.com/AkshantVats/lensai-integration (quickstart docker-compose + smoke.sh)
